claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (25 cases x 3 roles x 3 runs x 3 models)

links.outcome: LLM decision alignment with physician majority under stakeholder role-prompt variation
links.effect: Insurer role reduced alignment with physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4 (p = 0.004), 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (p = 0.008), and 10.5% (NS) for Opus 4.6.
links.quote: Among 20 cases with clear physician consensus, LLMs prompted as an insurer reduced alignment with physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4 (p = 0.004), 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (p = 0.008) and 10.5% (NS) for Opus 4.6.

unlisted_practices: Standardized LLM patient-centricity benchmarks (e.g., Patient-Centric Decision Index)

links.quote: Among 20 cases with clear physician consensus, LLMs prompted as an insurer reduced alignment with physician majority by 50% for GPT-5.4 (p = 0.004), 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (p = 0.008) and 10.5% (NS) for Opus 4.6.

links.effect: Insurer role produced systematic denial; alignment fell 50% for GPT-5.4, 45% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and 10.5% for Opus 4.6.
links.quote: Stakeholder role-prompting fundamentally alters clinical decisions and ethical value frameworks of frontier LLMs, with the insurer role producing systematic denial of physician-endorsed, patient-preferred treatments.
